From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC schedule & location options — Valexis (onsite vs virtual)

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call. We’re ready to pick concrete dates for a 1.5-day hands-on POC focused on prompt review, routing validation, and a short load rehearsal. A couple of quick items before we lock things in: room access and recording permissions (see attachment).

Proposed windows (PT):
- Option A: Tue 10 Aug (afternoon) + Wed 11 Aug (full day)
- Option B: Thu 12 Aug (full day) + Fri 13 Aug (morning)

Agenda highlights:
- Day 1: prompt review & route configuration, role-based access check
- Day 2: live traffic routing, KV/prefix cache validation, 2x short load tests (15–30m)

Logistics questions:
- Do you want this onsite at your SF office or a virtual/hybrid session? If onsite, we’ll need visitor badges and a point of contact for network access (we can run from our laptop stack or your guest network).
- Recording: we typically record screens for internal post-mortems. Any restrictions on recording or storing session clips?
- AV / room layout: we can bring a dedicated 1U GPU node for the load tests; if onsite we’ll need a table + power + 1 dedicated Ethernet drop. I attached the runbook and a suggested room layout.

Next steps: pick preferred window and onsite vs virtual. If you’re leaning onsite, can you loop in facilities so we can confirm room availability? I’ve cc’d our enablement lead Soojin.

Attaching: POC_Runbook_v1.pdf (runbook + checklist), room_layout_QSpace.png (suggested setup)

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0134

Hi Ben —

Thanks — Option A (10–11 Aug) works best for the team. We’d prefer onsite for the hands-on portion, but two of our directors (Alex and Priya) will join remotely for parts of Day 1. Can you support a hybrid setup?

A couple of facility notes: our SF office requires guest badges for external vendors and a sponsored Wi‑Fi account for devices that need Internet access. We’ll bring a facilities contact on the next note to confirm room booking and whether there’s an ethernet drop available.

Recording: We’re happy for recordings for technical follow-up, but anything with customer PII or sensitive prompts should be stopped/edited. We’ll provide a short consent form.

Tom — looping you for availability and any constraints on dataset snippets during the load test.

Emma — perfect, thanks for confirming Option A. We can absolutely run hybrid: will bring a compact GPU node and a laptop for screen share; we’ll also bring a preconfigured USB with the test prompts so we don’t need to send sensitive data over email.

To QSpace Facility (cc’d): can you confirm room availability for Tue 10 Aug (1:00pm–5:00pm) + Wed 11 Aug (9:00am–5:00pm)? Requirements: table for 4–6 people, projector or HDMI-capable display, one dedicated ethernet drop (or approved guest network with port access). If there’s a technical contact for the day, please share name and best number.

On recordings: We’ll mark start/stop manually and will not include any PII-bearing prompt dumps in the recorded sections. We’ll coordinate consent forms in advance — Emma, if you share the short consent doc I’ll circulate internally.

Sooj: can you own prompt-run hygiene and the 2x load-test windows? I’ll coordinate with facilities on logistics. Marissa will handle calendar invites and drive folder permissions.

Thanks —
Ben
